title: Kernel wakeup latency scratchpad
body:
Notes to self: kernel wakeup costs and effect on p99 at low qps

Context
- Problem: observed sporadic p99 spikes (~3-4x baseline) on small requests (<=128 tokens) when QPS is low-to-moderate (5-50r/s) and concurrency is 1-4 per container. Suspect: kernel wakeup latency and event loop wakeups on hotpath.
- Goal: measure contribution of user/kernel transition (wakeup) to end-to-end token latency and test mitigations (io_uring, epoll busy-wait, thread-pin, timer granularity).

Quick summary of experiments (dates recorded inline):
1) baseline (epoll + polite sleep) — 2025-10-05
   - harness: local-single-core container (c6g.large-like), 1 worker thread pinned to core 2, event loop using epoll_wait with 10ms timeout fallback.
   - load: 20r/s steady, payload: 40 tokens, mean server-side processing 6ms (mock).
   - observed: p50=21ms, p95=47ms, p99=120ms (spikes every ~30s)
   - notes: spikes correlate with periodic 10s GC-like workload in other thread — suggests cross-core wakeup penalty.

2) epoll busy-poll (SO_BUSY_POLL) enabled — 2025-10-12
   - kernel param set: net.core.busy_poll=50 (ops), socket busy poll on accept fds for 50us
   - observed: p50=19ms, p95=32ms, p99=60ms — big improvement on spikes but CPU up ~4%
   - tradeoff: higher CPU, less wakeup penalty. Good for dedicated pools.

3) switched to io_uring (liburing v2.5) — 2025-11-03
   - event loop rewired to submit/read with io_uring (sqe: readv/accept) + fixed-size SQ polling (ring->sq->poll) without timeouts.
   - observed: p50=18ms, p95=28ms, p99=42ms. CPU similar to epoll busy-poll but smoother tail.
   - artifact: a few OOMs if queue depth too low; need tuning for high concurrent accepts.

4) thread pinning + cgroup cpuset isolation — 2025-12-08
   - pinned IO thread and worker thread adjacent cores (core 2 and 3), isolated background threads to cores 6-7.
   - observed: p50=17ms, p95=25ms, p99=40ms. Spikes reduced frequency.

5) timer granularity / kernel tick tweaks (tickless) — 2026-01-19
   - tested CONFIG_NO_HZ and sched_wakeup_granularity_ns adjustments (lowered from 5000000 -> 500000 ns on test vm).
   - observed: minor gains; p99 improved by ~5-8% only. Hard to change in managed k8s clusters.

Microbench notes (how I measured)
- harness script (local): ./scripts/wakeup_probe.sh — spawns N client threads, requests with fixed payload, records RTT on client and server processing time on server.
- server logs include monotonic timestamps (CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW) at: accept, read-complete, queue-dequeue, request-start, request-end. Subtract queue-dequeue->request-start to isolate wakeup cost + scheduling jitter.
- ran perf (kernel) sampling on hot threads: perf record -e sched:sched_wakeup -g -p $PID -o perf.data
- also used 'ftrace' trace-points for sched_wakeup and sched_waking interactions; cheap but verbose.

Representative raw numbers (one run, 20r/s, 1 worker):
- avg scheduling latency (queue-dequeue -> request-start): 0.85ms
- 75th: 1.2ms
- 95th: 3.6ms
- 99th: 19.8ms (rare outliers correlated with cross-core migrations)

ASCII timeline (single spike)
[0ms] accept->enqueue -> (0.8ms) dequeue -> worker woke -> (0.004ms) start processing -> ...
then a spike trace:
[0ms] accept->enqueue -> (0.8ms) worker sleep -> sched_wakeup -> (15ms) worker scheduled on different core -> start processing

Hypothesis and root causes (working):
- cross-core wakeup penalty when target thread is parked deep-sleeping -> kernel must send IPI, scheduler picks core -> migration cost.
- epoll_wait with long timeout causes threads to park; wakeup pays full penalty.
- busy-poll reduces park frequency at cost of CPU.
- io_uring can use polling and submission queue polling to eliminate kernel userspace roundtrips for IO completions (reduces latency).

Mitigations tried and notes:
- SO_BUSY_POLL: works well for ephemeral low-latency workloads, but requires kernel support and increases CPU. Good candidate for Dedicated.
- io_uring: best tail behavior in my tests; need to ensure kernel >=5.11 and liburing stable. Also careful with CQE overflow and fixed buffers.
- thread pinning + cpuset: cheap wins, reduces cross-core migrations. Must ensure orchestration (kube) won't reschedule pods across nodes unexpectedly.
- busy-loop hybrid: spin for 100us then park — good compromise when expecting bursts but saves CPU relative to full busy-poll. Implemented as spin-yield loop in user-space.

Open questions / next runs
- test spin-then-park heuristic vs SO_BUSY_POLL on a fleet-like noise background (50% background CPU noise).
- measure impact on aggregated cost: e.g., 5% CPU -> X% cost increase vs tail reduction savings at customer-level SLOs. Need to simulate token mix and per-token cost model.
- confirm io_uring behaviour under heavy accept churn (benchmark 200 connections/s).
- can we upstream a small runtime flag (busy_poll:off|spin:100us|io_uring) for customers to toggle per-deployment? Add to rollout config.

Quick deployment notes
- busy_poll requires CAP_NET_ADMIN to change socket options on some platforms; need user-space fallback.
- io_uring requires recent kernel in Private deployments — note to solutions-engineering for installer checklist.

TODOs
- [ ] Run 3-day soak w/ io_uring on a dedicated pool and collect p99 cost tradeoffs (owner: Arjun)
- [ ] Add telemetry metric: wakeup_latency_ms histogram and correlate with cgroup cpuset shifts (owner: me)
- [ ] Draft short RFC for "wake-optimized runtime mode" and include knobs/expected CPU delta and gating for Dedicated only (owner: Rhea)

Random notes / snack ideas
- maybe adaptively toggle busy-poll on traffic patterns: enable busy-poll for first 30s after pod spin-up then revert.
- rough rule-of-thumb: if avg inter-arrival < 2ms then keep spin; otherwise park. Need to simulate.

End of scratchpad.

-- rhea
